A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent-ODE learning-rate scheduler and retain matching methods, experiments, and appendices. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and next-token prediction experiments, scheduler ablations, sharpness measurements, runtime comparisons, and reconstruction results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds numerical-solver diagnostics, reconstruction-sensitivity experiments, and latent-representation visualizations.

M1.justification: The three-metric input, latent dynamics, path-length regularization, and five scheduling steps remain unchanged. v2 newly documents the ODE-RNN encoder and omission of a variational penalty, without establishing a change from v1's implementation. Algorithm 1's indexing correction aligns it with the existing top-three selection described in the prose.

E1.justification: Both versions use Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and TinyStories for the same classification, next-token prediction, and training-trajectory modeling tasks. The added diagnostics examine retained datasets and tasks; they do not introduce new domains or test populations.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 explicitly adds use of Xiong et al.'s graph-based RL-controller implementation to the previously Xu-based setup. The single RL-controller row leaves the implementation's assignment across tasks incompletely specified. Other comparator families remain unchanged; 'Exp. Decay' becoming 'Step Decay' matches the implementation already described in v1 Appendix A.2.

E3.justification: The principal benchmark metrics, optimizers, and learning-rate sweeps are retained. New supplementary protocols vary solver tolerances from 1e-4 to 1e-6 and observed trajectory fractions from 1% to 100%, and sample latent encodings at ten points per epoch for UMAP analysis. Newly disclosed tokenizer and default solver settings do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive analyses of integration behavior and function evaluations, sensitivity to solver tolerance and observation fraction, and latent geometry across schedules and training phases (Figures A1–A3). Training-loss panels also extend the existing path and horizon analyses. The original configuration, horizon, and training-data ablations remain; v1's reconstruction Figure A1 is relocated to v2 Figure 2.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports two-sided t-tests comparing LODE with the next-best scheduler across all five model/dataset combinations, with p-values from 0.0001 to 0.01. The original means, standard deviations, and stated 20-seed or 10-seed benchmark reporting remain; no increase in those run counts is established.

E6.justification: New results include approximately 111 function evaluations per integrated trajectory, reconstruction curves across solver tolerances, latent-cluster patterns, and additional training-loss trajectories. Table 1 revises RL-controller CIFAR-100 accuracy from 71.0±1.0 to 73.9±0.9; Table 5 revises its runtime from 38.7±0.2 to 11.2±0.4 seconds. These accompany revised RL implementation documentation and should not be treated as demonstrated same-setting improvements. LODE's benchmark scores and the numerical results in Tables 2–4 and A1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the sample-acceptance condition, and the quadratic-loss edge-of-stability bound are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added empirical diagnostics introduce no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 replaces the abstract's SOTA claim with superiority over the evaluated baselines and removes the introduction's claim to be the first scheduling technique modeling training as a dynamical system. The conclusion ties the largest observed gain more explicitly to the transformer experiment. The central generative-scheduling and long-term-performance contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 more explicitly qualifies computational efficiency by estimating the upfront pipeline cost at roughly 100 complete training runs and identifying cost reduction as future work. Appendix A.3 discusses solver diagnostics in relation to potential latent-ODE stiffness. The principal exploration/convergence and flatter-minimum interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: ODE-RNN details, Diffrax/Tsit5 integration, PID control, tolerances, initial step size, and 64-bit precision; transformer tokenization, positional embeddings, feed-forward width, and normalization settings; and RL implementation provenance and offline training cost. It also points to supplementary lode_scheduler.py instead of only promising future code. However, v1's explicit eight-block/eight-head transformer specification is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work adds substantive discussions of Ding et al.'s ODE learning-curve extrapolation and Subramanian et al.'s sharp learning-rate transitions. A new 'Key distinctions' paragraph positions LODE's novelty around generating schedules, distinguishing it from ranking fixed schedules or applying restricted RL corrections. Solver and UMAP references are added, while two earlier RL references are removed.

P1.justification: The title and first author's printed surname change, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and cost discussion receive targeted revisions. Grammar and cross-references are corrected, and the reconstruction explanation moves into a new Section 5.1. The main section sequence and much of the methods and discussion remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different publication layout and substantially reorganizes displays. It moves the reconstruction figure into the main text, adds three appendix figures, adds training-loss panels to two existing analyses, transposes Table 3, and adds a significance row to Table 1. Accuracy-distribution plots incorporate RL-controller curves, and Table A1's CIFAR model label is corrected to ResNet18.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and assessment of the evidence through explicit numerical settings, solver-sensitivity checks, significance tests, and more carefully scoped performance and novelty claims. These strengthen the existing study. Some ambiguity remains in the aggregated RL-controller reporting, and the transformer description loses its explicit block/head counts. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
